text: All right. Thank you. So with regards to the property tax deferral program at the December 8th regular council meeting, council directed admin to look into the number of property tax and utility bill penalties being assessed for 2020, given the approval of the program to provide information on effectiveness of those measures. And if people in businesses were still in need of them, provide recommendations to extend or implement measures and provide recommendations to ensure that the penalty process is aligned with the intent of the deferral program. In response to this notice of motion, admin analyzed both current and arrears penalties imposed in 2020 and the two prior years and concluded on the effectiveness and if there is a need for further measures. Admin also reviewed the process on penalty dates and its alignment with the deferral program. It's admins understanding that the intent of this program was to provide immediate financial relief from a taxation perspective for those hardest hit by COVID-19. Shifting the due date for taxes from June 30th to September 30th, ease the burden of payment on this current 2020 balance for property taxes. The city's property tax penalty bylaw had penalty dates set for 30, 90 and 150 days after tax notices had been imposed for penalty amounts on the current year balance of six, three and 3% respectively. Bylaw also had penalty dates set for arrears balances, which includes all outstanding amounts regardless of the year for January 1st and April 1st. In order to align the penalties process with the deferral program, admin brought forward an amendment to this tax penalty bylaw to include verbiage unless otherwise directed by council. What this allowed administration to do is shift the penalty dates 90 days as well to align with the 90 day deferral on taxes, which can be seen outlined in the attachment on table eight. Each penalty date on current balances was deferred 90 days as I just stated. As the 150 day penalty on current year balances would be deferred into a future year, which would actually be February 1st of 2021, who is waived entirely as there's no current balance due yet in 2021. As part of the analysis, we looked at penalties on 2020 taxes. So to affirm the effectiveness of the deferral program, admin separated each type of penalty into two categories, current and arrears and performed analytics on each. The key indicator of the effectiveness being penalties on current balances. However, the finding on arrears balances is also worth noting, especially considering if further measures are required. On current balances, I'll draw your attention to table B, which is page 39 of 49. Administration compared the amount of penalties assessed at 30, 90 and 150 day intervals to both 2019 and 2018. The expectation is if the program was effective, the amount of penalties assessed would either be comparable or decrease. The data shows that in 2020, there was a significant decrease in the amount of penalties imposed on current balances. Admin was only required to report approximately half the penalties it does in normal year, which would indicate that a program was a large success. Performing analysis on the arrears balances, which would be December 31st, once again to two prior years, which is table C. If the ratio of current balances had substantially increased compared to prior years, it would be an indicator that the program was not as effective as intended and further measures may be required. As the outstanding balance on current years at December 31st, 2020 was the lowest of the three years, it's a good indicator that deferral program was effective in easing the tax burden on rate payers. Further, the overall arrears balance decreased from prior years which is another indicator that taxpayers have been able to avoid penalties better in 2020 than in prior years. It's admin's opinion that the deferral measures approved by council were effective. Looking at alignment of the penalty dates, once again, drawing your attention to table A, the penalty dates were shifted for 90 days or in the one case waived entirely, whereas the arrears penalties were not. The rationale for this is that arrears balances include balances on all tax years, not just 2020, would include 2019, 2018 and prior years as well. Significant portion, 36% of penalties imposed on arrears balances are for three years prior to 2020. Non-payment of these particular balances would be unrelated to the hardships from COVID-19. As the intent of the deferral program was to ease the burden impacted by COVID-19 in the 2020 year, current balances, existing bylaw dates were used for arrears penalties. The admin feels that this approach does align and does not recommend extension or implementation of further measures. In spite of this, there are approximately six months from the due date, which will be June 30th until the first arrears penalty date in a normal year, which would be January 1st of the following year. Should council feel that arrears penalty dates require further alignment with the intent of the program, an option is to shift the penalty date on the current 2020 portion of the arrears balances in a similar manner to current penalties. This would result in the 12% January 1st penalty being deferred until April 1st, and the April 1st penalty being deferred until July 1st on the 2020 amount outstanding. It is worth noting that adjusting these dates would require some retroactive adjustments and some significant admin time to implement. Based on the analysis discussed above, the data does not support that this is required. And for that reason, admin has not brought this forward as a recommendation. The budget financial impact on the 2020 operating budget includes an estimate for tax penalty revenue in the amount of 420,000. As noted above, the deferral measures resulted in a significant reduction in penalties in the amount of 91,000. Although this produces an unfavorable variance in terms of the budget, the benefit of the residents' ability to pay their outstanding balances reduces the administrative burden on the collection. text: Thank you, mayor and council. So this by-law is being brought forth within the parameters of the upcoming investment policy which will be presented to council in 2021. These strategies will increase the return the city receives on its reserve balances. However, this will reduce the city's liquid cash available.
